api.title: Device integration guide
api.intro: How an attendance terminal talks to Temari.et — three endpoints, one token, offline-first. The terminal keeps its branch's card list locally, decides every tap on the spot with no network, and syncs in the background. Cards are F08 NFC chips: the 4-byte UID, written as 8 uppercase hex characters, is the only identity the device ever handles. Every cadence below is exact — implement it as written.
api.authNote: No request carries a device ID — the token itself IS the device's identity, unique per terminal, so the server always knows which device (and which branch) is calling. A device can never read or write outside its own branch, and it never sees names, phones or any personal data.

provision.title: Register & provision
provision.body: Register the terminal on the Devices tab — its access token is shown exactly once. Write the token and the base URL into the device's own flash storage so they survive reboots and firmware updates. On the LILYGO T-SIM7670G-S3 store them in NVS via the serial provisioning console: plug in USB-C, open a serial terminal at 115200 baud, type the three commands, done.
provision.note: Never bake a token into the firmware image: every terminal runs the same firmware but carries its OWN token. If a token leaks, rotate it from the Devices tab — the old one dies instantly. One branch can run many terminals (one per gate); anyone in the branch can scan on any of them.

heartbeat.title: Phone home
heartbeat.body: Send a heartbeat once on boot and then every 5 minutes. It confirms the device is registered and enabled, powers the Online indicator in the panel, and returns two things: server_time — set the device clock from it on every single beat, a drifting clock silently turns "present" into "late" — and roster_version.
heartbeat.note: Compare roster_version with the version stored at the last roster sync. Different → run step 3 immediately. Identical → do nothing. A quiet day costs zero roster bytes, and a newly issued card starts working within 5 minutes.

roster.title: Sync the card list
roster.body: Pull the full list this terminal should accept: two flat arrays of card UIDs — students and employees — scoped to the device's branch and audience. A card is listed only while it is active AND its holder is still current: a lost card, a withdrawn student or a former employee disappears at the next sync. Replace the local table, store meta.version, done.
roster.note: Pull in exactly three cases: on first boot, immediately when a heartbeat's roster_version differs from the stored one, and one forced full pull every 24 hours even if the version matches. UIDs only — no names, no phones, nothing personal ever reaches the device.

gate.title: Verify at the gate — offline
gate.body: Every tap is decided locally: format the F08 card's 4-byte UID as 8 uppercase hex characters, look it up in the stored list, and accept or reject on the spot. Queue every tap either way as {uid, scanned_at} — rejected taps matter too: the server records them as unknown-card or lost-card attempts in the scan log, which is how a stolen card gets noticed.
gate.note: scanned_at must be ISO 8601 with a timezone offset (e.g. 2026-07-25T08:02:11+03:00). One record per tap — the server itself works out check-in vs check-out, present vs late.

upload.title: Upload the scan queue
upload.body: Every 5 minutes, send the oldest 500 queued scans in one request (fewer if the queue is shorter; skip the cycle if it is empty). Each event is just uid + scanned_at — the server derives its own duplicate-proof id from them, so the device numbers nothing and re-sending an entire backlog after an offline stretch is always safe. Delete the sent records only when the response status is 200; on any other status keep the queue untouched and retry at the next 5-minute cycle.
upload.note: Two taps of the same card in the same second collapse into one event — free debounce. Attendance is derived asynchronously; per-scan outcomes appear in the Scan log tab.

recover.title: Errors & recovery
recover.e401: 401 — the token is unknown, rotated, or the device was disabled from the panel. Keep verifying and queuing scans locally; retry the upload every few minutes.
recover.e422: 422 — malformed payload: missing uid or scanned_at, or more than 500 events in one batch. Fix the request; never discard the queue.
recover.queue: Never delete unsent scans. The events endpoint swallows duplicates, so replaying the entire local queue after connectivity returns is always safe.

storage.title: Small terminals (8–16 MB storage): plenty, if stored right
storage.t1: Store the roster as a sorted binary table (~8 bytes per card) and binary-search it — 15,000 cards is ~120 KB and every lookup is instant. Parse the JSON once on sync, then throw it away.
storage.t2: Keep the scan queue as fixed-size records in a ring file, deleted only after the upload is acknowledged — a full day of 30,000 scans is about 1 MB.
storage.t3: Send Accept-Encoding: gzip — the roster compresses ~10×, so even a 10,000-person branch syncs in under 100 KB of mobile data.

share.title: Public share link
share.hint: Share this exact guide with someone outside the panel — a firmware engineer, a vendor. The link shows the docs and nothing else: no data, no accounts, no API access. Generating a new link kills the old one instantly; Disable turns sharing off altogether.
share.rotated: New link generated — the old link is dead.
share.invalidTitle: This link is no longer active
share.invalidHint: The link was rotated or disabled. Ask Temari.et for a fresh one.
share.disableWarning: The link stops working immediately for everyone who has it. You can generate a new one anytime.
